scope: Independent AI-assisted semantic review of all six completed schema-v3.1 development responses, including summaries, claims, retrieved definitions, actual recorded tool results, SQL, warnings and citations.
method: Direct semantic reading plus independent arithmetic from recorded result inputs; response hashes and every finding field/scale and claim citation mapping verified without importing application calculation helpers.
limitations: This is AI-assisted independent review, not human review, a replacement for the official human-review template, or a release approval. The official human review template and benchmark/source artifacts remain untouched.

Grounding assessed against the supplied frozen recorded evidence. Raw transaction/event records were not independently regenerated, provider transcripts were not re-run, and UI rendering/warning visibility was not checked.

The development run has only three questions with two systems each. These six response-level observations do not establish held-out generalization, production readiness, or results for the separately running full-v2 benchmark.
All six reviewed responses contain generated answers with completed status. No withheld/blocked answer was treated as semantic success.
Full-response criteria include the retrieved contracts, findings and warnings. Standalone narrative improvements are recorded separately rather than concealing this scope.

reviews.question: Why did activation fall last week?

wording_caveats.text: Within-group activation rates actually increased slightly in both acquisition channels
wording_caveats.issue: “Slightly” has no declared practical-size threshold. The direction is correct; neutral “increased” or the actual changes would be more precise.

wording_caveats.text: between the two documented signup cohorts
wording_caveats.issue: State the explicit September 1–8 and September 8–15, 2026 signup windows and seven-day activation in the summary so it stands alone.

notes: The response uses seven-day activation among eligible signup cohorts. Executed SQL enforces September 1 <= signup < September 8 and September 8 <= signup < September 15, 2026 UTC, with full seven-day maturity at the September 30 cutoff. Completion requires a matching practice-session start, not merely an unordered completion event.
329/600 versus 198/600 independently reconciles to 54.833333% versus 33.0%, a -21.833333 percentage-point change.

The country-independent channel decomposition uses symmetric average-rate/average-weight terms. Recomputed mix=-26.625 pp and within=+4.7916667 pp sum to -21.8333333 pp. Paid share rises from 20% to 80%; its activation rate is below organic in both periods.
The narrative calls this arithmetic accounting and the response warning explicitly denies causal interpretation. It does not establish why channel shares changed, nor claim to do so.

Window criterion passes only against this benchmark’s retrieved fixed-window contract. The relative phrase “last week” is not independently resolved to the current calendar week; the actual dates should be made explicit when presenting this answer.
The claim that both channel rates increased is supported: organic +5.625 pp and paid +3.958333 pp.

reviews.question: Evaluate the onboarding_valid A/B experiment.

wording_caveats.text: The observed difference in completion rates between treatment and control is very small
wording_caveats.issue: The observed +1 pp is supported, but “very small” is a judgment without a declared material-effect threshold. Prefer “The observed difference is +1 pp”; retain the wide confidence interval.
p-values are dimensionless; render “SRM p = 1” instead of a trailing “p” unit.
The findings identify the interval as 95%; repeat 95% and the seven-day outcome in the summary for standalone clarity.

notes: The cited contract specifies the onboarding_valid user-level fixed-horizon experiment and intent-to-treat completion within seven days of assignment. SQL keeps mature assignments and preserves noncompleters with the left join.
Control=171/300=57%; treatment=174/300=58%; treatment-control=+1 pp. Recomputed 95% Newcombe score interval is [-6.8714481,+8.8539771] pp; recomputed 50:50 chi-square SRM p=1.
“No allocation imbalance was detected” is appropriately limited to the SRM result. It does not claim that balanced allocation proves correct randomization or overall experiment validity.
“Inconclusive evidence of an effect” correctly follows from an interval spanning zero. The answer does not assert equivalence, prove no effect, or recommend rollout.
The response warning retains the fixed-horizon, single-binary-outcome scope and unmeasured-guardrail limitation. This review has not verified UI visibility of that warning.

reviews.question: Which countries contributed to the sales change?

wording_caveats.text: the sales increase between the two months
wording_caveats.issue: Name October to November 2011 and “gross positive sales” in the summary. Those qualifiers currently require the retrieved definition/findings/warnings.

notes: The requested contribution question is answered for October versus November 2011 gross positive sales in GBP, as defined by the retrieved contract and executed arguments.
All 29 country before/after pairs and deltas reconcile. Country sums equal October GBP 1,154,979.30 and November GBP 1,509,496.33; total change is GBP 354,517.03.

UK GBP +386,371.20 is the largest positive contribution. Japan +6,512.04, EIRE +6,420.51 and Norway +2,840.27 are supported positives; Netherlands -14,834.64, Australia -9,907.81 and Singapore -7,067.32 are supported negatives.

The narrative calls this accounting decomposition. The response warning also expressly rules out causal explanation and states the positive-quantity/price, cancellation exclusion, retained-duplicate and missing-customer-ID policies.
No net-revenue, profit, causal-uplift, visits, activation or experiment claims are made. The summary is a useful selection of countries; all 29 contributions remain available in evidence/findings.
